security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG or helper iterates vector element operations (vadd.vv, vle8.v, vse8.v) up to vlmax (VLEN/SEW/LMUL) instead of CSR vl actual value, causing writes to destination vector register elements beyond the configured vector length that the guest expects to remain undisturbed per tail-agnostic/tail-undisturbed policy
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: vector loop bound uses vlmax or VLEN/SEW-derived maximum instead of env->vl or CSR vl; missing vl-based early termination in vext_ldst_us, vext_ldst_stride, or vector arith helpers; vstart not added to element index in memory address calculation for unit-stride loads/stores
security_spec.summary: Vector instruction emulation must iterate exactly CSR[vl] elements (not vlmax) and apply CSR[vstart] offset to source/dest bit positions, otherwise QEMU corrupts tail elements the guest kernel's undisturbed policy protects, breaking vector register isolation between guest processes

findings.finding: Vector VV operation loop bound uses vl=env->vl (line 71: for i=env->vstart; i<vl; i++). total_elems used only for tail element initialization (line 81). No vlmax-derived maximum is used as loop bound.
Vector VX operation loop bound uses vl=env->vl (line 97: for i=env->vstart; i<vl; i++). total_elems only used for tail initialization.

Strided load/store loop bound correctly uses env->vl (line 322). max_elems (VLEN/SEW-derived) used only for multi-field element indexing within register groups, not as loop bound. Memory address calculation (line 332) correctly uses stride * i with i starting from vstart.

Unit-stride load/store takes evl parameter (passed env->vl from GEN_VEXT_LD_US at line 518-519), not vlmax. Address calculation at line 462: addr = base + ((env->vstart * nf) << log2_esz) correctly includes vstart in the address offset.
Indexed load/store loop bound uses env->vl (line 604). get_index_addr reads index value from vs2 at position i (starting from vstart), correctly using element index to compute memory address.

Fault-only-first load correctly uses env->vl as loop bound throughout (lines 697, 701, 706, 711, 754, 777, 785). First element fault allowed, subsequent elements probed non-fault. Address calculation at line 697: addr = base + ((env->vstart * nf) << log2_esz) correctly includes vstart.

Whole-register load/store correctly uses vlenb for element count (evl = nf * vlenb >> log2_esz), which is spec-correct: whole-register instructions always operate on the entire register group regardless of vl.

Floating-point VV helper loop bound uses ecrp->vl=env->vl (line 3155). total_elems from vext_get_total_elems() correctly accounts for EEW/SEW/LMUL differences and is used only for tail element initialization.
gvec fast-path only activates when vl_eq_vlmax is true (vl == vlmax), so using MAXSZ(s) as gvec size is safe. When vl != vlmax, falls through to the helper path where loop uses env->vl.

All remaining vector operations (compare, mask-adc, mask-set, iota, vid, vcpop, mask logical) use env->vl as the primary loop bound and total_elems only for tail element initialization. No instance found where vlmax/vext_max_elems is used as element iteration bound.
